sections.overview: Pangasius sanitwongsei is a very large freshwater catfish native to the Mekong and Chao Phraya basins in Southeast Asia.
sections.identification: FishBase reports a maximum length near 3 metres; despite the nickname “paroon shark,” it is a catfish, not a shark.
sections.habitat: Adults use large rivers and juveniles larger tributaries; the species migrates within river systems.
sections.diet: Accounts report that young and adults eat fish and crustaceans, although detailed field observations are limited.
sections.behavior: Dams and modified river flows can obstruct its migrations and alter cues used for movement and spawning.
sections.reproduction: Mekong River Commission reports place spawning in upper river reaches before or during the early monsoon; timing varies among stretches.
sections.ecology: It belongs to Pangasiidae but is distinct from the better-known Mekong giant catfish Pangasianodon gigas, a different genus in the same family.
sections.conservation: The IUCN assessment lists it as Critically Endangered, citing overfishing and disruption of river migration and spawning habitat; Viet Nam also prioritizes it for protection.
